pages.title: Two Kinds of Power
pages.text: There are two kinds of power in this mod:$(br)$(li)$(item)Alternating current (AC)$(): generated and used on the spot, measured in EP/s. It is a rate, not a store of energy; every machine that needs to be powered runs on it.$(li)$(item)Direct current (DC)$(): stored in batteries and carried by items, measured in EP. It can charge batteries and the Electric Whisk, or be converted into AC.

pages.title: AC/DC Converter
pages.text: This machine converts between the two kinds of power. It has an internal buffer of 3 000 EP of direct current and a battery slot.$(br2)Conversion: 1 EP = 10 FE (which is what other mods see as RF, AE and so on).

pages.title: Mode One: AC to DC
pages.text: The default mode. The converter scans one block to each of its $(l)left and right sides$() (the two directions perpendicular to its facing); if it finds an AC generator there, such as a Faraday Generator or a Wind Turbine Controller, it harvests their AC, subtracts the loss and stores the result in its buffer or in the battery slot to the right.$(br2)In this mode it can also take supply from a Tesla Coil to produce DC.

pages.title: Mode Two: DC to AC
pages.text: Switch the mode button to DC-to-AC and the converter pulls power from the battery (or its own buffer) and turns it into AC that a Tesla Coil can use.$(br2)It consumes $(thing)working speed × 10 EP$() of DC per second and outputs the same EP/s. A speed of 50 therefore means 500 EP/s of AC output.$(br2)The AC it makes must be taken by a Tesla Coil right next to it — otherwise it goes nowhere.

pages.title: Speed and Loss
pages.text: Working speed decides the conversion efficiency: the higher the speed the greater the absolute power, but the $(l)proportional loss$() grows too. What actually arrives is generation × (1 − speed ÷ (3 × maximum speed)).$(br2)The maximum speed is 50 by default (changeable in the config), so speed 0 loses nothing, speed 20 keeps 86.7%% and speed 50 keeps only 66.7%%.$(br2)Click the buttons in the interface to change it by 1, or hold Shift to change it by 5.

pages.title: When to Use It
pages.text: $(li)To power electric appliances from solar panels: they make only DC, so it must be converted to AC and handed to a Tesla Coil.$(li)To "bank" a power grid: convert AC to DC to fill batteries, then switch back to DC-to-AC when you need it.
